recognize_zh: 視野中央一顆比紅血球大約兩倍的淋巴球，細胞核圓、染色質濃縮，周圍有較豐富的淡藍色細胞質，內含數顆散在的粗大紫紅色嗜天青顆粒（azurophilic granules），即大顆粒淋巴球。
features: Single lymphocyte roughly twice the diameter of a red cell with a low-to-intermediate N:C ratio
Round to slightly indented nucleus with condensed, clumped chromatin and no visible nucleolus
Abundant pale blue cytoplasm with irregular outline
Several coarse, discrete azurophilic granules scattered in the cytoplasm
Background red cells with scattered crenated forms (echinocytes, likely drying artifact) and occasional platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large lymphocyte with a round, mature-appearing nucleus with condensed chromatin and abundant pale blue cytoplasm containing several coarse azurophilic granules. The background red cells include scattered crenated forms, most likely artifactual. Findings are consistent with a large granular lymphocyte; a single LGL is a normal finding, and a diagnosis of LGL leukemia requires a sustained increase (typically >2 x 10^9/L) with demonstration of clonality by flow cytometry and TCR studies.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have deeply basophilic cytoplasm that hugs adjacent red cells and usually lack discrete azurophilic granules.
Monocytes have folded or kidney-shaped nuclei with lacy chromatin and grey-blue cytoplasm with fine dust-like granules and vacuoles.
Hairy cells have oval nuclei with open chromatin and circumferential fine cytoplasmic projections without azurophilic granules.
Alder-Reilly granules are dark and present in all leukocyte lineages, including neutrophils, rather than only in a subset of lymphocytes.
